react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 9.6×10⁻¹⁵), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 1.6×10⁻⁸), and mummichog m/z-network activity (p = 1.7×10⁻⁴) — converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / WP:WP465) as the overwhelmingly dominant affected pathway. Six tryptophan-derived metabolites drove this signal: L-tryptophan (C00078), its decarboxylation product tryptamine (C00398), the decarboxylated aldehyde indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), the kynurenine-pathway intermediate 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and the two serotonin-pathway end-products serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598). The Reactome pathway Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931) was also independently enriched (FDR 6.6×10⁻⁸), capturing the L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin arm. Acrolein (C01471) and doxycycline (C06973) are xenobiotics not mapped to the tryptophan cluster by any tool. Cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (C00127) is annotated as glutathione disulfide by mummichog; the KEGG compound ID appears in the ascorbate/aldarate and linoleate metabolism network branches but with low specificity and no cross-paradigm confirmation. The biological story is a broad perturbation of tryptophan catabolism, with the strongest signal in the neurotransmitter branch producing serotonin and melatonin. Milrinone (C07224) is a phosphodiesterase inhibitor without a tryptophan connection in any pathway database. No cross-paradigm consensus was reached for arachidonic acid, cytokine, purine, or cardiac drug pathways.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms—RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network activity—converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the top-affected pathway. RaMP reports FDR 9.58×10⁻¹⁵ (rank 1/10 KEGG), MetaboAnalystR reports p = 1.59×10⁻⁸ (rank 1 KEGG), and mummichog reports p = 1.68×10⁻⁴ (rank 1 MUMM). Within this pathway, six tryptophan-derived metabolites are significantly altered: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632), tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and melatonin (KEGG:C01598). A sub-pathway of serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) is also significantly enriched (FDR 6.64×10⁻⁸) and contains L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. Reactome further confirms biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550) and amino acid metabolism (WP:WP3925) hits. The metabolite C00127, submitted as cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, maps to glutathione disulfide (CHEBI:17858) in both mummichog and the ChEBI resolver; its annotation is ambiguous. Doxycycline (KEGG:C06973), acrolein (KEGG:C01471), and milrinone (KEGG:C07224) do not map to any tryptophan-cluster pathway in any paradigm. The biological signal is therefore centred on tryptophan catabolism, specifically its decarboxylation branch to tryptamine and its oxidation branch through 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid to the kynurenine-NAD⁺ sink, with serotonin and melatonin at the neurotransmitter terminus.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a dominant biological signal centred on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380). RaMP-DB multi-database ORA identifies Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR 9.58e-15, rank 1 KEGG), with six metabolites mapping to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine.   "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a dominant biological signal centred on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380). RaMP-DB multi-database ORA identifies Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR 9.58e-15, rank 1 KEGG), with six metabolites mapping to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently recovers the same pathway with p = 1.59e-08 (rank 1 KEGG), hitting an identical six-metabolite set. Mummichog m/z-network activity confirms the signal as the top MUMM-ranked hit (p = 8.40e-05), with seven resolved metabolites from the input mapping to tryptophan metabolism. This cross-paradigm consensus is further supported by Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 6.64e-08) and Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550, FDR 6.64e-08) as validated secondary hits in the RaMP ORA. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA identifies Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (FDR 9.58e-15, rank 1 KEGG), with six metabolites mapping to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently recovers the same pathway with p = 1.59e-08 (rank 1 KEGG), hitting an identical six-metabolite set. Mummichog m/z-network activity confirms the signal as the top MUMM-ranked hit (p = 8.40e-05), with seven resolved metabolites from the input mapping to tryptophan metabolism. The driver metabolite set for the primary signal is L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), which feeds into both the serotonin-melatonin neurotransmitter arm and the 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid kynurenine branch of tryptophan catabolism, with tryptophan 5-monooxygenase (EC 1.14.16.4) and N-acetylserotonin O-acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.87) as key branch-point enzymes.
